translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 130

sentences.zh: 【宋紀十二】　旃蒙大荒落，一年。

translations.literal: [Song Records 12] From Zhanmeng Dahuangluo; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Song Records 12] From Zhanmeng Dahuangluo—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 太宗明皇帝上之上泰始元年（

translations.literal: Upper Part One of Emperor Ming the Filial, Taishi year 1 (
translations.idiomatic: Upper Part One of Emperor Ming the Filial, Taishi year 1 (

sentences.zh: 乙巳，公元四六五年）

translations.literal: yisi, equivalent to 465 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yisi, equivalent to 465 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未朔，廢帝改元永光，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the yiwei new moon, the Deposed Emperor changed the era name to Yongguang and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yiwei new moon, Emperor Qianfei changed the era name to Yongguang and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，魏主如樓煩宮。

translations.literal: In the second month, on dingchou, the Wei ruler went to the Loufan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingchou, the Northern Wei emperor went to the Loufan Palace.

sentences.zh: 自孝建以來，民間盜鑄濫錢，商貨不行。

translations.literal: Since the Xiaojian era, the people had illicitly cast debased coin, and trade in goods did not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xiaojian era, the people had illicitly cast debased coin, and commerce had stalled.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，更鑄二銖錢，形式轉細。

translations.literal: On gengyin, new two-zhu coins were cast, their form becoming ever finer.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the court recast two-zhu coins, but their form grew ever finer.

sentences.zh: 官錢每出，民間即模效之，而更薄小，無輪郭，不磨鑢，謂之「耒子。」

translations.literal: Whenever official coin was issued, the people at once imitated it, making pieces yet thinner and smaller, without rims or filing, and called them "Leizi."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever official coin left the mint, the people at once counterfeited it, making pieces yet thinner and smaller, without rims or filing, and called them "Leizi."

sentences.zh: 三月，乙巳，魏主還平城。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yisi, the Wei ruler returned to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yisi, the Northern Wei emperor returned to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，癸卯，魏高宗殂。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on guimao, Wei's Emperor Gaozong died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on guimao, Northern Wei's Emperor Wencheng died.

sentences.zh: 初，魏世祖經營四方，國頗虛耗，重以內難，朝野楚楚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei's Emperor Shizu had campaigned in all directions; the state was greatly depleted, and with internal troubles added, court and countryside were in distress.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei had campaigned in all directions; the state was greatly depleted, and with internal troubles added, court and countryside were in distress.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣之，與時消息，靜以鎮之，懷集中外，民心復安。

translations.literal: Gaozong succeeded him, adapting to the times, calming affairs through stillness, winning over Chinese and foreigners alike, and the people's hearts were again at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng succeeded him, adapting to the times, calming affairs through stillness, winning over Chinese and foreigners alike, and the people's hearts were again at peace.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，太子弘即皇帝位，大赦，尊皇后日皇太后。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the crown prince Hong assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and honored the empress as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Crown Prince Hong assumed the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and honored the empress as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時年十二，侍中、車騎大將軍乙渾專權，矯詔殺尚書楊保年、平陽公賈愛仁、南陽公張天度於禁中。

translations.literal: Xianzu was then twelve years old. The attendant-in-ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun monopolized power and, by forged edict, killed the Minister of Works Yang Baonian, the Duke of Pingyang Jia Airen, and the Duke of Nanyang Zhang Tiandu within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen was then twelve years old. Attendant-in-ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry Yi Hun monopolized power and, by forged edict, killed Minister of Works Yang Baonian, Duke of Pingyang Jia Airen, and Duke of Nanyang Zhang Tiandu within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 侍中、司徒、平原王陸麗治疾於代郡溫泉，乙渾使司衛監穆多侯召之。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-ordinary, Minister over the Masses, and Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li was treating his illness at the hot springs in Dai commandery; Yi Hun sent the Director of Palace Guards Mu Duohou to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-ordinary, Minister over the Masses, and Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li was treating his illness at the hot springs in Dai commandery; Yi Hun sent Director of Palace Guards Mu Duohou to summon him.

sentences.zh: 多侯謂麗曰：「渾有無君之心。

translations.literal: Duohou said to Li: "Hun harbors a heart that disowns the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou said to Li, "Hun harbors treasonous intent toward the throne.

sentences.zh: 今宮車晏駕，王德望素重，奸臣所忌，宜少淹留以觀之；

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage has halted forever. Your Highness's virtue and standing have long been weighty, and the traitor will resent you. You ought to linger a while to observe how things stand;
translations.idiomatic: Now the late emperor has passed. Your virtue and standing have long been weighty, and the traitor will resent you. You ought to linger a while and watch how things develop;

sentences.zh: 朝廷安靜，然後入，未晚也。」

translations.literal: once the court is calm, then enter the capital—it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: once the court has settled, then enter the capital—it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 麗曰：「安有聞君父之喪，慮患而不赴者乎！」

translations.literal: Li said: "How could there be one who, hearing of his lord and father's death, weighs danger and does not hasten to attend!"
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "How could anyone who hears of his lord and father's death weigh danger and fail to hasten there!"

sentences.zh: 即馳赴平城。

translations.literal: He at once galloped to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He at once galloped to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 乙渾所為多不法，麗數爭之。

translations.literal: Yi Hun's conduct was largely unlawful, and Li repeatedly disputed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Hun's conduct was largely unlawful, and Li repeatedly disputed him.

sentences.zh: 戊申，渾又殺麗及穆多侯。

translations.literal: On wushen, Hun again killed Li and Mu Duohou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Hun again killed Li and Mu Duohou.

sentences.zh: 多侯，壽之弟也。

translations.literal: Duohou was the younger brother of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou was the younger brother of Mu Shou.

sentences.zh: 己酉，魏以渾為太尉、錄尚書事，東安王劉尼為司徒，尚書左僕射代人和其奴為司空。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Wei appointed Hun Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Prince of Dong'an Liu Ni as Minister over the Masses; and the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Daihe Helu, as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Northern Wei appointed Hun Grand Commandant and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Dong'an Liu Ni as Minister over the Masses; and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Helu of Daihe as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書順陽公郁謀誅乙渾，渾殺之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Secretariat, the Duke of Shunyang Yu, plotted to kill Yi Hun; Hun killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Duke of Shunyang Yu plotted to kill Yi Hun; Hun killed him.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏以淮南王它為鎮西大將軍、儀同三司，鎮涼州。

translations.literal: On renzi, Wei appointed the Prince of Huainan Ta Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Palace Attendant of the First Rank, to garrison Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Northern Wei appointed Prince of Huainan Tuoba Ta Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Palace Attendant of the First Rank, to garrison Liang province.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏開酒禁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wei lifted the ban on wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Northern Wei lifted the ban on wine.

sentences.zh: 壬午，加柳元景南豫州刺史，加顏師伯丹陽尹。

translations.literal: On renwu, Liu Yuanjing was additionally made Governor of Southern Yu province, and Yan Shibo was additionally made Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Liu Yuanjing was additionally appointed Governor of Southern Yu province, and Yan Shibo was additionally appointed Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸巳，魏以太尉乙渾為丞相，位居諸王上；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, Wei made the Grand Commandant Yi Hun Chancellor, ranking above all the princes;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on guisi, Northern Wei made Grand Commandant Yi Hun Chancellor, ranking above all the princes;

sentences.zh: 事無大小，皆決於渾。

translations.literal: matters great and small were all decided by Hun.
translations.idiomatic: matters great and small were all decided by Hun.

sentences.zh: 廢帝幼而狷暴。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor had been headstrong and violent from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei had been headstrong and violent from childhood.

sentences.zh: 及即位，始猶難太后、大臣及戴法興等，未敢自恣。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, he still feared the empress dowager, the great ministers, and Dai Faxing and others, and did not dare indulge himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the throne, he still feared the empress dowager, the great ministers, and Dai Faxing and others, and did not dare indulge himself.

sentences.zh: 太后既殂，帝年漸長，欲有所為，法興輒抑制之，謂帝曰：「官所為如此，欲作營陽邪！」

translations.literal: After the empress dowager died, the emperor gradually grew older and wished to act as he pleased, but Faxing repeatedly restrained him, saying to the emperor: "Your Majesty acts thus—do you wish to become another Emperor Yang of Yingyang!"
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, the emperor gradually grew older and wished to act as he pleased, but Faxing repeatedly restrained him, saying, "Your Majesty acts thus—do you wish to become another Emperor Yang of Yingyang!"

sentences.zh: 帝稍不能平。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually could not contain his resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually could not contain his resentment.

sentences.zh: 所幸閹人華願兒，賜與無算，法興常加裁減，願兒恨之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Huayuan'er, whom he favored, received gifts beyond counting, but Faxing often cut them back, and Huayuan'er hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Huayuan'er, whom he favored, received gifts beyond counting, but Faxing often cut them back, and Huayuan'er hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝使願兒於外察聽風謠，願兒言於帝曰：「道路皆言『宮中有二天子：法興為真天子，官為贗天子。』

translations.literal: The emperor sent Huayuan'er abroad to listen to popular rumors. Huayuan'er said to the emperor: "On the roads everyone says, 'In the palace there are two Sons of Heaven: Faxing is the true Son of Heaven, and Your Majesty is the counterfeit Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Huayuan'er abroad to listen to popular rumors. Huayuan'er said to the emperor, "On the roads everyone says, 'In the palace there are two Sons of Heaven: Faxing is the real emperor, and Your Majesty is the fake one.

sentences.zh: 且官居深宮，與人物不接，法興與太宰、顏、柳共為一體，往來門客恆有數百，內外士庶莫不畏服。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty dwells deep within the palace and has little contact with others, while Faxing, the Grand Tutor, Yan, and Liu form a single bloc; their visiting clients are constantly in the hundreds, and gentlemen and commoners within and without all fear and submit to them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty dwells deep within the palace and has little contact with others, while Faxing, the Grand Tutor, Yan, and Liu form a single bloc; their visiting clients constantly number in the hundreds, and gentlemen and commoners within and without all fear and submit to them.

sentences.zh: 法興是孝武左右，久在宮闈；

translations.literal: Faxing was a confidant of Emperor Xiaowu and had long been in the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: Faxing was a confidant of Emperor Xiaowu and had long been in the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 今與它人作一家，深恐此坐席非復官有。」

translations.literal: now he has joined with others as one household—I deeply fear this seat is no longer Your Majesty's alone."
translations.idiomatic: now he has joined with others as one household—I deeply fear this throne is no longer yours alone."

sentences.zh: 帝遂發詔免法興，遣還田裡，仍徙遠郡。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict dismissing Faxing, sending him back to his home district, and then exiling him to a distant commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon issued an edict dismissing Faxing, sending him back to his home district, and then exiling him to a distant commandery.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛酉，賜法興死，解巢尚之舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on xinyou, Faxing was sentenced to death, and Chao Shangzhi was removed as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinyou, the emperor ordered Faxing to take his own life, and Chao Shangzhi was removed as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 員外散騎侍郎東海奚顯度，亦有寵於世祖。

translations.literal: Xi Xiandu of Donghai, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, had also enjoyed favor under Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xiandu of Donghai, Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary, had also enjoyed favor under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 常典作役，課督苛虐，捶撲慘毒，人皆苦之。

translations.literal: He regularly oversaw corvée labor, imposing levies with harsh cruelty and beating people with appalling severity; all suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly oversaw corvée labor, imposing levies with harsh cruelty and beating people with appalling severity; all suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 帝常戲曰：「顯度為百姓患，比當除之。」

translations.literal: The emperor often jested, saying: "Xiandu is a scourge upon the people; before long he should be removed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often jested, saying, "Xiandu is a scourge upon the people; before long he should be removed."

sentences.zh: 左右因唱諾，即宣旨殺之。

translations.literal: His attendants thereupon chorused assent and at once proclaimed the imperial will to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants thereupon chorused assent and at once proclaimed the imperial will to kill him.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射、領衛尉卿、丹陽尹顏師伯居權日久，海內輻湊，驕奢淫恣，為衣冠所疾。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrent Commandant of the Guards, and Intendant of Danyang, had held power for a long time; the realm converged upon him. He was arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute, and the gentry detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrent Commandant of the Guards, and Intendant of Danyang, had held power for a long time; the realm converged upon him. He was arrogant, extravagant, and dissolute, and the gentry detested him.

sentences.zh: 帝欲親朝政，庚午，以師伯為尚書左僕射，解卿、尹，以吏部尚書王彧為右僕射，分其權任。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to take the government into his own hands. On gengwu, he made Shibo Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and relieved him of his posts as Commandant and Intendant; he made Wang Yu of the Ministry of Personnel Right Vice Director, dividing Shibo's power and duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to take the government into his own hands. On gengwu, he made Shibo Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and relieved him of his posts as Commandant and Intendant; he made Wang Yu of the Ministry of Personnel Right Vice Director, dividing Shibo's power and duties.

sentences.zh: 師伯始懼。

translations.literal: Shibo began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo began to fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖多猜忌，王公、大臣，重足屏息，莫敢妄相過從。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Shizu was greatly suspicious; princes, dukes, and great ministers walked as if on tiptoe and held their breath, not daring to visit one another casually.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Xiaowu was greatly suspicious; princes, dukes, and great ministers walked as if on tiptoe and held their breath, not daring to visit one another casually.

sentences.zh: 世祖殂，太宰義恭等皆相賀曰：「今日始免橫死矣！」

translations.literal: When Shizu died, the Grand Tutor Yigong and the others all congratulated one another, saying: "Today we have at last escaped sudden death!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor Yigong and the others all congratulated one another, saying, "Today we have at last escaped sudden death!"

sentences.zh: 甫過山陵，義恭與柳元景、顏師伯等聲樂酣飲，不捨晝夜；

translations.literal: Hardly had the imperial tomb rites passed when Yigong, together with Liu Yuanjing, Yan Shibo, and the rest, feasted on music and wine day and night without cease;
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the imperial tomb rites passed when Yigong, together with Liu Yuanjing, Yan Shibo, and the rest, feasted on music and wine day and night without cease;

sentences.zh: 帝內不能平。

translations.literal: inwardly the emperor could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: inwardly the emperor could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 既殺戴法興，諸大臣無不震懾，各不自安；

translations.literal: After Dai Faxing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to be shaken with fear; each felt insecure;
translations.idiomatic: After Dai Faxing was killed, none of the great ministers failed to be shaken with fear; each felt insecure;

sentences.zh: 於是元景、師伯密謀廢帝，立義恭，日夜聚謀，而持疑不能決。

translations.literal: thereupon Yuanjing and Shibo secretly plotted to depose the emperor and set up Yigong. Night and day they gathered to scheme, yet hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: thereupon Yuanjing and Shibo secretly plotted to depose the emperor and set up Yigong. Night and day they gathered to scheme, yet hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 元景以其謀告沈慶之；

translations.literal: Yuanjing disclosed their plot to Shen Qingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing disclosed their plot to Shen Qingzhi;

sentences.zh: 慶之與義恭素不厚，又師伯常專斷朝事，不與慶之參懷，謂令史曰：「沈公，爪牙耳，安得預政事！」

translations.literal: Qingzhi had never been close to Yigong, and moreover Shibo often monopolized court affairs and did not consult Qingzhi, saying to a clerk: "Master Shen is merely a fang and claw—how may he take part in government!"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi had never been close to Yigong, and moreover Shibo often monopolized court affairs and did not consult Qingzhi, saying to a clerk, "Master Shen is merely a fang and claw—how may he take part in government!"

sentences.zh: 慶之恨之，乃發其事。

translations.literal: Qingzhi hated him for this and thereupon exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi hated him for this and thereupon exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝自帥羽林兵討義恭，殺之，並其四子。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the emperor himself led the Palace Guard to attack Yigong, killed him, and killed his four sons as well.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, the emperor himself led the Palace Guard to attack Yigong, killed him, and killed his four sons as well.

sentences.zh: 斷絕義恭支體，分裂腸胃，挑取眼睛，以蜜漬之，謂之「鬼目粽」。

translations.literal: He severed Yigong's limbs, split open his belly, scooped out his eyes, and pickled them in honey, calling the result "Ghost-Eye Zongzi."
translations.idiomatic: He severed Yigong's limbs, split open his belly, scooped out his eyes, and pickled them in honey, calling the result "Ghost-Eye Zongzi."

sentences.zh: 別遣使者稱詔召柳元景，以兵隨之。

translations.literal: He separately sent an envoy bearing a forged edict to summon Liu Yuanjing, with troops following behind.
translations.idiomatic: He separately sent an envoy bearing a forged edict to summon Liu Yuanjing, with troops following behind.

sentences.zh: 左右奔告「兵刃非常」。

translations.literal: His attendants ran to tell him that "the weapons were extraordinary."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants ran to tell him that "the weapons were extraordinary."

sentences.zh: 元景知禍至，入辭其母，整朝服乘車應召。

translations.literal: Yuanjing knew disaster had come. He went in to bid farewell to his mother, straightened his court robes, mounted his carriage, and answered the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing knew disaster had come. He went in to bid farewell to his mother, straightened his court robes, mounted his carriage, and answered the summons.

sentences.zh: 弟車騎司馬叔仁戎服，帥左右壯士欲拒命，元景苦禁之。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Cavalry Commandant Shuren, donned armor and wished to lead stalwart followers to resist the order, but Yuanjing sternly forbade him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Cavalry Commandant Shuren, donned armor and wished to lead stalwart followers to resist the order, but Yuanjing sternly forbade him.

sentences.zh: 既出巷，軍士大至。

translations.literal: Once he had left the lane, soldiers arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had left the lane, soldiers arrived in force.

sentences.zh: 元景下車受戮，容色恬然；

translations.literal: Yuanjing descended from his carriage to receive execution, his bearing serene;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing descended from his carriage to receive execution, his bearing serene;

sentences.zh: 並其八子、六弟及諸侄。

translations.literal: he was killed together with his eight sons, six younger brothers, and all his nephews.
translations.idiomatic: he was killed together with his eight sons, six younger brothers, and all his nephews.

sentences.zh: 獲顏帥伯於道，殺之，並其六子。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo was seized on the road and killed, together with his six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo was seized on the road and killed, together with his six sons.

sentences.zh: 又殺廷尉劉德願。

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice Liu Deyuan was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Liu Deyuan was also killed.

sentences.zh: 改元景和，文武進位二等。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Jinghe, and civil and military officials were advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Jinghe, and civil and military officials were advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 遣使誅湘州刺史江夏世子伯禽。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to execute Boqin, heir of Jiangxia and Governor of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to execute Boqin, heir of Jiangxia and Governor of Xiang province.

sentences.zh: 自是公卿以下，皆被捶曳如奴隸矣。

translations.literal: From this time forth, everyone from the highest ministers down was beaten and dragged about like slaves.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forth, everyone from the highest ministers down was beaten and dragged about like slaves.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在東宮，多過失，世祖欲廢之而立新安王子鸞，侍中袁覬盛稱「太子好學，有日新之美」，世祖乃止；

translations.literal: Earlier, while the emperor was crown prince, he had many faults. Emperor Shizu wished to depose him and set up the Prince of Xin'an, Ziluan. The attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Kan greatly praised him, saying "The crown prince loves learning and has the beauty of daily renewal," and Shizu thereupon desisted;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was crown prince, he had many faults. Emperor Xiaowu wished to depose him and set up Prince of Xin'an Ziluan. Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Kan greatly praised him, saying "The crown prince loves learning and has the beauty of daily renewal," and Xiaowu thereupon desisted;

sentences.zh: 帝由是德之。

translations.literal: the emperor therefore felt gratitude toward him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor therefore felt gratitude toward him.

sentences.zh: 既誅群公，欲引進覬，任以朝政，遷為吏部尚書，與尚書左丞徐爰皆以誅義恭等功，賜爵縣子。

translations.literal: After the great lords were executed, he wished to advance Kan and entrust him with court government, promoting him to Minister of Personnel. Both Kan and the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Ai were ennobled as Viscount of a county for their merit in executing Yigong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: After the great lords were executed, he wished to advance Kan and entrust him with court government, promoting him to Minister of Personnel. Both Kan and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Ai were ennobled as Viscount of a county for their merit in executing Yigong and the others.

sentences.zh: 徐爰便僻善事人，頗涉書傳，自元嘉初，入侍左右，豫參顧問；

translations.literal: Xu Ai was facile and obsequious, skilled at pleasing others, and had some acquaintance with books and records. From the beginning of the Yuanjia era he entered service at the ruler's side and took part in counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai was facile and obsequious, skilled at pleasing others, and had some acquaintance with books and records. From the beginning of the Yuanjia era he entered service at the ruler's side and took part in counsel;

sentences.zh: 既長於附會，又飾以典文，故為太祖所任遇。

translations.literal: being adept at ingratiation and adorning himself with classical texts, he was therefore entrusted and favored by Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: being adept at ingratiation and adorning himself with classical texts, he was therefore entrusted and favored by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 大明之世，委寄尤重。

translations.literal: In the Daming era his commission was especially weighty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era his commission was especially weighty.

sentences.zh: 時殿省舊人多見誅逐，唯爰巧於將迎，始終無迕；

translations.literal: At that time many old hands of the palace offices were executed or driven out, but Ai alone was skilled at courting favor and from first to last met with no offense;
translations.idiomatic: At that time many old hands of the palace offices were executed or driven out, but Ai alone was skilled at courting favor and from first to last met with no offense;

sentences.zh: 廢帝待之益厚，群臣莫及。

translations.literal: the Deposed Emperor treated him all the more generously, and no minister could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei treated him all the more generously, and no minister could compare.

sentences.zh: 帝每出，常與沈慶之及山陰公主同輦，爰亦預焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out, he commonly shared a carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin, and Ai also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went out, he commonly shared a carriage with Shen Qingzhi and the Princess of Shanyin, and Ai also took part.

sentences.zh: 山陰公主，帝姊也，適駙馬都尉何戢。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shanyin was the emperor's elder sister and was married to the Commandant of Cavalry He Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanyin was the emperor's elder sister and was married to Commandant of Cavalry He Zhan.

sentences.zh: 戢，偃之子也。

translations.literal: Zhan was the son of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was the son of He Yan.

sentences.zh: 公主尤淫恣，嘗謂帝曰：「妾與陛下，男女雖殊，俱托體先帝。

translations.literal: The princess was especially licentious and willful. She once said to the emperor: "Your servant and Your Majesty, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was especially licentious and willful. She once said to the emperor, "Your servant and Your Majesty, though man and woman differ, both owe our bodies to the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 陛下六宮萬數，而妾唯駙馬一人，事太不均。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's six palaces number in the tens of thousands, yet your servant has only one commandant of cavalry—this is far too unequal."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's six palaces number in the tens of thousands, yet your servant has only one commandant of cavalry—this is far too unequal."

sentences.zh: 帝乃為公主置面首左右三十人，進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon set up thirty male favorites at the princess's left and right, advanced her to Princess of Kuaiji commandery with the rank of a commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon set up thirty male favorites at the princess's left and right, advanced her to Princess of Kuaiji commandery with the rank of a commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎褚淵貌美，公主就帝請以自侍，帝許之。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel was handsome in appearance; the princess approached the emperor and asked that he serve her personally, and the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel was handsome in appearance; the princess approached the emperor and asked that he serve her personally, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 淵侍公主十日，備見逼迫，以死自誓，乃得免。

translations.literal: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was subjected to every pressure, and swore he would die rather than submit—only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan attended the princess for ten days, was subjected to every pressure, and swore he would die rather than submit—only then was he released.

sentences.zh: 淵，湛之之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan was the son of Zhanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was the son of Chu Zhanzhi.

sentences.zh: 帝令太廟別畫祖考之像，帝入廟，指高祖像曰：「渠大英雄，生擒數天子。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered separate portraits of the ancestral emperors painted in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Entering the temple, he pointed at the portrait of the Founder and said: "That fellow was a great hero—he captured several Sons of Heaven alive."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered separate portraits of the ancestral emperors painted in the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Entering the temple, he pointed at the portrait of the Founder and said, "That fellow was a great hero—he captured several emperors alive."

sentences.zh: 指太祖像曰：「渠亦不惡，但末年不免兒斫去頭。」

translations.literal: He pointed at the portrait of Taizu and said: "That fellow was not bad either, but in his last years he could not escape having his head chopped off by his son."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at the portrait of Emperor Wen and said, "That fellow was not bad either, but in his last years he could not escape having his head chopped off by his son."

sentences.zh: 指世祖像曰：「渠大齇鼻。

translations.literal: He pointed at the portrait of Shizu and said: "That fellow has a great pug nose.
translations.idiomatic: He pointed at the portrait of Emperor Xiaowu and said, "That fellow has a great pug nose.

sentences.zh: 如何不齇？」

translations.literal: Why is it not pug?"
translations.idiomatic: Why is it not pug?"

sentences.zh: 立召畫工令齇之。

translations.literal: He at once summoned the painter and ordered him to make it pug.
translations.idiomatic: He at once summoned the painter and ordered him to paint a pug nose.

sentences.zh: 以建安王休仁為雍州刺史，湘東王彧為南豫州刺史，皆留不遣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Governor of Yong province, and the Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made Governor of Southern Yu province; both were kept at court and not sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Governor of Yong province, and Prince of Xiangdong Yu was made Governor of Southern Yu province; both were kept at court and not sent out.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以司徒、揚州刺史、豫章王子尚領尚書令。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, the Minister over the Masses, Governor of Yang province, and Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was made concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Minister over the Masses, Governor of Yang province, and Prince of Yuzhang Zishang was made concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以始興公沈慶之為侍中、太尉；

translations.literal: On yihai, the Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Duke of Shixing Shen Qingzhi was made attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 慶之固辭。

translations.literal: Qingzhi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 征青、冀二州刺史王玄謨為領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Wang Xuamo, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, was summoned to serve as General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuamo, Governor of Qing and Ji provinces, was summoned to serve as General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 魏葬文成皇帝於金陵，廟號高宗。

translations.literal: Wei buried the Literary-Cultured Emperor at Jinling; his temple name was Gaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei buried Emperor Wencheng at Jinling; his temple name was Gaozong.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸巳，帝如湖熟，戊戌，還建康。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guisi, the emperor went to Hushu; on wuxu he returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guisi, the emperor went to Hushu; on wuxu he returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 新安王子鸞有寵於世祖，帝疾之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xin'an, Ziluan, had enjoyed favor under Emperor Shizu, and the emperor resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin'an Ziluan had enjoyed favor under Emperor Xiaowu, and the emperor resented him.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，遣使賜子鸞死，又殺其母弟南海王子師及其母妹，發殷貴妃墓；

translations.literal: On xinchou, an envoy was sent to order Ziluan to take his own life. The emperor also killed his younger brother by the same mother, the Prince of Nanhai Zishi, and his mother's younger sister, and opened the tomb of the Honored Consort Yin;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, an envoy was sent to order Ziluan to take his own life. The emperor also killed his younger brother by the same mother, Prince of Nanhai Zishi, and his mother's younger sister, and opened the tomb of Honored Consort Yin;

sentences.zh: 又欲掘景寧陵，太史以為不利於帝，乃止。

translations.literal: he also wished to excavate the Jingning Mausoleum, but the court astronomers said it would be inauspicious for the emperor, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: he also wished to excavate the Jingning Mausoleum, but the court astronomers said it would be inauspicious for the emperor, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 初，金紫光祿大夫謝莊為殷貴妃《誄》曰：「贊軌堯門。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Xie Zhuang had written a dirge for the Honored Consort Yin, saying: "Praising the tracks at the Gate of Yao."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Household Counsellor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon Xie Zhuang had written a dirge for Honored Consort Yin, saying, "Praising the tracks at the Gate of Yao."

sentences.zh: 帝以莊比貴妃於鉤弋夫人，欲殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor, taking Zhuang's comparison of the consort to Lady Gouyi, wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taking Zhuang's comparison of the consort to Lady Gouyi, wished to kill him.

sentences.zh: 或說帝曰：「死者人之所同，一往之苦，不足為困。

translations.literal: Someone advised the emperor: "Death is what all men share alike; the suffering of a single passage is not enough to be called hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised the emperor, "Death is what all men share alike; the suffering of a single passage is not enough to be called hardship.

sentences.zh: 莊生長富貴，今系之尚方，使知天下苦劇，然後殺之，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Zhuang was born and raised in wealth and honor. Now bind him in the Imperial Workshop and let him know the world's bitter trials—then kill him; it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was born and raised in wealth and honor. Now bind him in the Imperial Workshop and let him know the world's bitter trials—then kill him; it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史義陽王昶，素為世祖所惡，民間每訛言昶當反；

translations.literal: The Prince of Yiyang Chang, Governor of Xu province, had long been detested by Emperor Shizu, and among the people rumors constantly said Chang would rebel;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yiyang Liu Chang, Governor of Xu province, had long been detested by Emperor Xiaowu, and among the people rumors constantly said Chang would rebel;

sentences.zh: 是歲，訛言尤甚。

translations.literal: that year the rumors were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: that year the rumors were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 廢帝常謂左右曰：「我即大位以來，遂未嘗戒嚴，使人邑邑！」

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor often said to his attendants: "Since I took the great throne, I have never once proclaimed martial law—how it makes one restless!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei often said to his attendants, "Since I took the throne, I have never once proclaimed martial law—how it makes one restless!"

sentences.zh: 昶使典簽蘧法生奉表詣建康，求入朝，帝謂法生曰：「義陽與太宰謀反，我正欲討之。

translations.literal: Chang sent his registrar Qu Fasheng to present a memorial at Jiankang requesting an audience. The emperor said to Fasheng: "Yiyang is plotting rebellion with the Grand Tutor—I was just about to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent his registrar Qu Fasheng to present a memorial at Jiankang requesting an audience. The emperor said to Fasheng, "Yiyang is plotting rebellion with the Grand Tutor—I was just about to attack him.

sentences.zh: 今知求還，甚善！」

translations.literal: Now that I know he wishes to return, that is excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that I know he wishes to return, that is excellent!"

sentences.zh: 又屢詰問法生：「義陽謀反，何故不啟？」

translations.literal: He repeatedly pressed Fasheng with questions: "Yiyang is plotting rebellion—why did you not report it?"
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pressed Fasheng with questions, "Yiyang is plotting rebellion—why did you not report it?"

sentences.zh: 法生懼，逃還彭城；

translations.literal: Fasheng was afraid and fled back to Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng was afraid and fled back to Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 帝因此用兵。

translations.literal: the emperor thereupon mobilized troops.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor thereupon mobilized troops.

sentences.zh: 己酉，下詔討昶，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict was issued to attack Chang, and martial law was proclaimed within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, an edict was issued to attack Chang, and martial law was proclaimed within and without.

sentences.zh: 帝自將兵渡江，命沈慶之統諸軍前驅。

translations.literal: The emperor himself led troops across the river and ordered Shen Qingzhi to command all armies as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself led troops across the river and ordered Shen Qingzhi to command all armies as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 法生至彭城，昶即聚兵反；

translations.literal: When Fasheng reached Pengcheng, Chang at once gathered troops and rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: When Fasheng reached Pengcheng, Chang at once gathered troops and rebelled;

sentences.zh: 移檄統內諸郡，皆不受命，斬昶使，將佐文武悉懷異心。

translations.literal: he issued a proclamation to all commanderies under his jurisdiction, but none accepted his orders. Chang's envoys were beheaded, and all his civil and military officers harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: he issued a proclamation to all commanderies under his jurisdiction, but none accepted his orders. Chang's envoys were beheaded, and all his civil and military officers harbored divided loyalties.

sentences.zh: 昶知事不成，棄母、妻，攜愛妾，夜與數十騎開北門奔魏。

translations.literal: Chang knew the affair could not succeed. He abandoned his mother and wife, took his favorite concubine, and in the night, with several dozen horsemen, opened the north gate and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chang knew the affair could not succeed. He abandoned his mother and wife, took his favorite concubine, and in the night, with several dozen horsemen, opened the north gate and fled to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 昶頗涉學，能屬文。

translations.literal: Chang had considerable learning and could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had considerable learning and could compose literary pieces.

sentences.zh: 魏人重之，使尚公主，拜侍中、征南將軍、駙馬都尉，賜爵丹陽王。

translations.literal: The people of Wei valued him, had him marry an imperial princess, and appointed him attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Conquers the South, and Commandant of Cavalry, ennobling him as Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei valued him, had him marry an imperial princess, and appointed him attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Conquers the South, and Commandant of Cavalry, ennobling him as Prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書袁覬，始為帝所寵任，俄而失指，待遇頓衰，使有司糾奏其罪，白衣領職。

translations.literal: Yuan Kan, Minister of Personnel, had at first been favored and entrusted by the emperor, but soon lost his footing; his treatment abruptly declined, and he was made to hold office in plain dress while the authorities investigated and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kan, Minister of Personnel, had at first been favored and entrusted by the emperor, but soon lost his footing; his treatment abruptly declined, and he was made to hold office in plain dress while the authorities investigated and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 覬懼，詭辭求出。

translations.literal: Kan was afraid and, with specious words, sought a post outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was afraid and, with specious words, sought a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以覬為督雍、梁等四州諸軍事、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Kan was made Commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yong, Liang, and four other provinces, and Governor of Yong province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Kan was made Commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Yong, Liang, and four other provinces, and Governor of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 覬舅蔡興宗謂之曰：「襄陽星惡，何可往？」

translations.literal: Kan's maternal uncle Cai Xingzong said to him: "The star of Xiangyang is ill-omened—how can you go there?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan's maternal uncle Cai Xingzong said to him, "The star of Xiangyang is ill-omened—how can you go there?"

sentences.zh: 覬曰：「『白刃交前，不救流矢。』

translations.literal: Kan said: "'When naked blades cross before you, one does not ward off stray arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "'When naked blades cross before you, one does not ward off stray arrows.

sentences.zh: 今者之行，唯願生出虎口耳。

translations.literal: On this journey I only wish to escape the tiger's jaws alive.
translations.idiomatic: On this journey I only wish to escape the tiger's jaws alive.

sentences.zh: 且天道遼遠，何必皆驗！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Way of Heaven is remote—why must every omen be fulfilled!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Way of Heaven is remote—why must every omen be fulfilled!"

sentences.zh: 是時，臨海王子頊為都督荊、湘等八州諸軍事、荊州剌史，朝廷以興宗為子頊長史、南郡太守，行府、州事，興宗辭不行。

translations.literal: At this time the Prince of Linhai, Zixu, was Commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing, Xiang, and eight other provinces and Governor of Jing province. The court wished to make Xingzong his chief administrator, Administrator of Nan commandery, and acting director of the princely establishment and provincial affairs, but Xingzong declined and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince of Linhai Zixu was Commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing, Xiang, and eight other provinces and Governor of Jing province. The court wished to make Xingzong his chief administrator, Administrator of Nan commandery, and acting director of the princely establishment and provincial affairs, but Xingzong declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 覬說興宗曰：「朝廷形勢，人所共見。

translations.literal: Kan urged Xingzong, saying: "The court's situation is plain to all.
translations.idiomatic: Kan urged Xingzong, saying, "The court's situation is plain to all.

sentences.zh: 在內大臣，朝不保夕，舅今出居陝西，為八州行事，覬在襄、沔，地勝兵強，去江陵咫尺，水陸流通。

translations.literal: The great ministers within the capital cannot be sure of living from morning to night. Uncle, you are now going out to dwell in the west of Shanxi as director of eight provinces' affairs, while I am at Xiang and Mian—superior terrain and strong troops, only a hand's breadth from Jiangling, with water and land routes in communication.
translations.idiomatic: The great ministers within the capital cannot be sure of living from morning to night. Uncle, you are now going out to dwell in the west of Shanxi as director of eight provinces' affairs, while I am at Xiang and Mian—superior terrain and strong troops, only a hand's breadth from Jiangling, with water and land routes in communication.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷有事，可以共立桓、文之功，豈比受制凶狂、臨不測之禍乎？

translations.literal: If the court has trouble, we can together establish achievements like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen—how is that compared with being controlled by a vicious madman and facing unforeseen disaster?
translations.idiomatic: If the court has trouble, we can together establish achievements like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen—how is that compared with being controlled by a vicious madman and facing unforeseen disaster?

sentences.zh: 今得間不去，後復求出，豈可得邪！」

translations.literal: If you do not go now when you have the chance, and later seek a post outside again, how could you obtain it!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not go now when you have the chance, and later seek a post outside again, how could you obtain it!"

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「吾素門平進，與主上甚疏，未容有患。

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "I am of a plain household that rose by regular promotion and am very distant from the ruler—I am not likely to incur trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said, "I am of a plain household that rose by regular promotion and am very distant from the ruler—I am not likely to incur trouble.

sentences.zh: 宮省內外，人不自保，會應有變。

translations.literal: Within and without the palace offices, no one can protect himself—there will surely be upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without the palace offices, no one can protect himself—there will surely be upheaval.

sentences.zh: 若內難得弭，外釁未必可量。

translations.literal: If internal troubles can be quelled, external disturbances may still be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: If internal troubles can be quelled, external disturbances may still be beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 汝欲在外求全，我欲居中免禍，各行其志，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: You wish to preserve yourself outside; I wish to avoid disaster at the center—each following his own intent—is that not also good!"
translations.idiomatic: You wish to preserve yourself outside; I wish to avoid disaster at the center—each following his own intent—is that not also good!"

sentences.zh: 覬於是狼狽上路，猶慮見追，行至尋陽，喜曰：「今始免矣。」

translations.literal: Kan thereupon set out on the road in disarray, still fearing pursuit. When he reached Xunyang he rejoiced, saying: "Now at last I am safe."
translations.idiomatic: Kan thereupon set out on the road in disarray, still fearing pursuit. When he reached Xunyang he rejoiced, saying, "Now at last I am safe."

sentences.zh: 鄧琬為晉安王子勳鎮軍長史、尋陽內史，行江州事。

translations.literal: Deng Wan was chief administrator to the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun, Military Governor, and Administrator of Xunyang, acting director of Jiang province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was chief administrator to Prince of Jin'an Zixun, Military Governor, and Administrator of Xunyang, acting director of Jiang province affairs.

sentences.zh: 覬與之款狎過常，每清閒，必盡日窮夜。

translations.literal: Kan was intimate with him beyond the usual degree; whenever they had leisure they would pass whole days and entire nights together.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was intimate with him beyond the usual degree; whenever they had leisure they would pass whole days and entire nights together.

sentences.zh: 覬與琬人地本殊，見者知其有異志矣。

translations.literal: Kan and Wan were utterly unlike in birth and station; those who saw them knew they harbored a separate design.
translations.idiomatic: Kan and Wan were utterly unlike in birth and station; those who saw them knew they harbored a separate design.

sentences.zh: 尋復以興宗為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xingzong was again made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xingzong was again made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 戊午，解嚴。

translations.literal: On wuwu, martial law was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, martial law was lifted.

sentences.zh: 帝因自白下濟江至瓜步。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon crossed the river from Baixia to Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon crossed the river from Baixia to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 沈慶之復啟聽民私鑄錢，由是錢貨亂敗。

translations.literal: Shen Qingzhi again memorialized to permit the people to cast coin privately, and thereby currency fell into chaos and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi again memorialized to permit the people to cast coin privately, and thereby currency fell into chaos and ruin.

sentences.zh: 千錢長不盈三寸，大小稱此，謂之「鵝眼錢」；

translations.literal: A thousand coins strung together did not fill three inches in length; pieces of this size were called "goose-eye coin";
translations.idiomatic: A thousand coins strung together did not fill three inches in length; pieces of this size were called "goose-eye coin";

sentences.zh: 劣於此者，謂之「綖環錢」；

translations.literal: those inferior to these were called "thread-ring coin";
translations.idiomatic: those inferior to these were called "thread-ring coin";

sentences.zh: 貫之以縷，入水不沉，隨手破碎。

translations.literal: strung on thread, they would not sink in water and broke apart at a touch.
translations.idiomatic: strung on thread, they would not sink in water and broke apart at a touch.

sentences.zh: 市井不復料數，十萬錢不盈一掬，斗米一萬，商貨不行。

translations.literal: In the markets people no longer counted by measure; a hundred thousand coins did not fill one handful; a dou of rice cost ten thousand, and trade in goods ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the markets people no longer counted by measure; a hundred thousand coins did not fill one handful; a dou of rice cost ten thousand, and trade in goods ceased.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙寅，帝還建康。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, the emperor returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingyin, the emperor returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 帝舅東陽太守王藻尚世祖女臨川長公主。

translations.literal: The emperor's maternal uncle Wang Zao, Administrator of Dongyang, had married the daughter of Emperor Shizu, the Princess of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's maternal uncle Wang Zao, Administrator of Dongyang, had married the daughter of Emperor Xiaowu, the Princess of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 公主妒，譖藻於帝。

translations.literal: The princess was jealous and slandered Zao to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was jealous and slandered Zao to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 己卯，藻下獄死。

translations.literal: On jimao, Zao was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Zao was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守孔靈符，所至有政績；

translations.literal: Kong Lingfu, Administrator of Kuaiji, wherever he served had administrative achievements;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Lingfu, Administrator of Kuaiji, wherever he served had administrative achievements;

sentences.zh: 以忤犯近臣，近臣譖之，帝遣使鞭殺靈符，並誅其二子。

translations.literal: because he offended a favorite minister, the favorite slandered him, and the emperor sent an envoy to whip him to death and also executed his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: because he offended a favorite minister, the favorite slandered him, and the emperor sent an envoy to whip him to death and also executed his two sons.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍何邁，瑀之子也，尚帝姑新蔡長公主。

translations.literal: He Mai, General Who Pacifies the North, was the son of Yu and had married the emperor's paternal aunt, the Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He Mai, General Who Pacifies the North, was the son of He Yu and had married the emperor's paternal aunt, the Princess of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 帝納公主於後宮，謂之謝貴嬪；

translations.literal: The emperor took the princess into the rear palace and called her Honored Consort Xie;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the princess into the rear palace and called her Honored Consort Xie;

sentences.zh: 詐言公主薨，殺宮婢，送邁等殯葬，行喪禮。

translations.literal: he falsely announced that the princess had died, killed a palace maid, and sent Mai and others to conduct the funeral and perform mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: he falsely announced that the princess had died, killed a palace maid, and sent Mai and others to conduct the funeral and perform mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，拜貴嬪為夫人。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Honored Consort was invested as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the Honored Consort was invested as Lady.

sentences.zh: 加鸞輅龍旂，出警入蹕。

translations.literal: She was given the imperial carriage with dragon banners and escorts clearing the road on her exits and entries.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the imperial carriage with dragon banners and escorts clearing the road on her exits and entries.

sentences.zh: 邁素豪俠，多養死士。

translations.literal: Mai had always been bold and chivalrous and kept many men willing to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Mai had always been bold and chivalrous and kept many men willing to die for him.

sentences.zh: 謀因帝出遊，廢之，立晉安王子勳。

translations.literal: He plotted that when the emperor went out on excursion, they would depose him and set up the Prince of Jin'an, Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted that when the emperor went out on excursion, they would depose him and set up Prince of Jin'an Zixun.

sentences.zh: 事洩，十一月，壬辰，帝自將兵誅邁。

translations.literal: The affair leaked out. In the eleventh month, on renchen, the emperor himself led troops to execute Mai.
translations.idiomatic: The affair leaked out. In the eleventh month, on renchen, the emperor himself led troops to execute Mai.

sentences.zh: 初，沈慶之既發顏、柳之謀，遂自暱於帝，數盡言規諫，帝浸不悅。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Shen Qingzhi had exposed the plot of Yan and Liu, he drew close to the emperor himself and repeatedly spoke out in full counsel and remonstrance, and the emperor gradually grew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Shen Qingzhi had exposed the plot of Yan and Liu, he drew close to the emperor himself and repeatedly spoke out in full counsel and remonstrance, and the emperor gradually grew displeased.

sentences.zh: 慶之懼禍，杜門不接賓客。

translations.literal: Qingzhi feared disaster and shut his gates, refusing to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi feared disaster and shut his gates, refusing to receive guests.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣左右范羨至吏部尚書蔡興宗所，興宗使羨謂慶之曰：「公閉門絕客，以避悠悠請托者耳。

translations.literal: He once sent his attendant Fan Xian to the residence of Cai Xingzong, Minister of Personnel. Xingzong had Xian tell Qingzhi: "Your Lordship shuts your gates and cuts off guests only to avoid the endless stream of petitioners.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent his attendant Fan Xian to the residence of Cai Xingzong, Minister of Personnel. Xingzong had Xian tell Qingzhi, "Your Lordship shuts your gates and cuts off guests only to avoid the endless stream of petitioners.

sentences.zh: 如興宗，非有求於公者也，何為見拒！」

translations.literal: As for Xingzong, I have no request to make of Your Lordship—why am I refused!"
translations.idiomatic: As for Xingzong, I have no request to make of Your Lordship—why am I refused!"

sentences.zh: 慶之使羨邀興宗。

translations.literal: Qingzhi had Xian invite Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi had Xian invite Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 興宗往見慶之，因說之曰：「主上比者所行，人倫道盡；

translations.literal: Xingzong went to see Qingzhi and thereupon urged him, saying: "The ruler's recent conduct has exhausted the way of human relations;
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong went to see Qingzhi and thereupon urged him, saying, "The ruler's recent conduct has exhausted the way of human relations;

sentences.zh: 率德改行，無可復望。

translations.literal: to lead him back to virtue and change his ways—there is nothing more to hope for.
translations.idiomatic: to lead him back to virtue and change his ways—there is nothing more to hope for.

sentences.zh: 今所忌憚，唯在於公；

translations.literal: What he now fears and dreads is only Your Lordship;
translations.idiomatic: What he now fears and dreads is only Your Lordship;

sentences.zh: 百姓喁喁，所瞻賴者，亦在公一人而已。

translations.literal: the people murmur, and the one they look to and rely upon is also Your Lordship alone.
translations.idiomatic: the people murmur, and the one they look to and rely upon is also Your Lordship alone.

sentences.zh: 公威名素著，天下所服。

translations.literal: Your Lordship's martial renown has long been established, and all under Heaven submit to it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Lordship's martial renown has long been established, and all under Heaven submit to it.

sentences.zh: 今舉朝遑遑，人懷危怖。

translations.literal: Now the whole court is in alarm; every man harbors dread and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole court is in alarm; every man harbors dread and fear.

sentences.zh: 指麾之日，誰不響應！

translations.literal: On the day you give the command, who would not answer!
translations.idiomatic: On the day you give the command, who would not answer!

sentences.zh: 如猶豫不斷，欲坐觀成敗，豈推旦暮及禍，四海重責將有所歸！

translations.literal: If you hesitate and cannot decide, wishing to sit and watch how success or failure unfold, can you put off disaster for even a morning or evening? The heavy responsibility of the four seas will fall upon someone!
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and cannot decide, wishing to sit and watch how success or failure unfold, can you put off disaster for even a morning or evening? The heavy responsibility of the four seas will fall upon someone!

sentences.zh: 僕蒙眷異常，故敢盡言，願公詳思其計。」

translations.literal: Your servant has received extraordinary favor and therefore dares speak fully—I beg Your Lordship to consider this plan carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has received extraordinary favor and therefore dares speak fully—I beg Your Lordship to consider this plan carefully."

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「僕誠知今日憂危，不復自保，但盡忠奉國，始終以之，當委任天命耳。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Your servant truly knows that today brings worry and peril and that I can no longer protect myself, but to devote loyalty to the state from first to last—that I shall do, and leave the rest to fate.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "Your servant truly knows that today brings worry and peril and that I can no longer protect myself, but to devote loyalty to the state from first to last—that I shall do, and leave the rest to fate.

sentences.zh: 加老退私門，兵力頓闕，雖欲為之，事亦無成。」

translations.literal: Moreover, I am old and have retired to my private gate; my military strength is suddenly depleted. Even if I wished to act, the affair could not succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I am old and have retired to my private gate; my military strength is suddenly depleted. Even if I wished to act, the affair could not succeed."

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「當今懷謀思奮者，非欲邀功賞富貴，正求脫朝夕之死耳！

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "Those who now harbor designs and think of rising up do not seek merit, reward, wealth, or honor—they only seek to escape death from morning to evening!
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said, "Those who now harbor designs and think of rising up do not seek merit, reward, wealth, or honor—they only seek to escape death from morning to evening!

sentences.zh: 殿中將帥，唯聽外間消息，若一人唱首，則俯仰可定。

translations.literal: The generals and commanders in the palace halls only await news from outside; if one man takes the lead, the realm can be settled in an instant.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and commanders in the palace halls only await news from outside; if one man takes the lead, the realm can be settled in an instant.

sentences.zh: 況公統戎累朝，舊日部曲，布在宮省，受恩者多，沈修之輩皆公家子弟耳，何患不從！

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Lordship has commanded armies for many reigns; your old retainers are posted throughout the palace offices, and many have received your grace. Men like Shen Xiuzhi are all your household's younger kinsmen—why fear they would not follow!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Lordship has commanded armies for many reigns; your old retainers are posted throughout the palace offices, and many have received your grace. Men like Shen Xiuzhi are all your household's younger kinsmen—why fear they would not follow!

sentences.zh: 且公門徒、義附，並三吳勇士。

translations.literal: Moreover, your disciples and sworn followers are all warriors of the Three Wu regions.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your disciples and sworn followers are all warriors of the Three Wu regions.

sentences.zh: 殿中將軍陸攸之，公之鄉人，今入東討賊，大有鎧仗，在青溪未發。

translations.literal: The Palace General Lu Youzhi is a fellow townsman of Your Lordship. He is now entering the east to attack rebels and has a great store of armor and weapons at Qingxi, not yet departed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace General Lu Youzhi is a fellow townsman of Your Lordship. He is now entering the east to attack rebels and has a great store of armor and weapons at Qingxi, not yet departed.

sentences.zh: 公取其器仗以配衣麾下，使陸攸之帥以前驅，僕在尚書中，自當帥百僚按前代故事，更簡賢明以奉社稷，天下之事立定矣。

translations.literal: Take his weapons and armor to equip the troops under your command, have Lu Youzhi lead them as vanguard, and your servant, within the Masters of Writing, will himself lead the hundred officials according to the precedents of former ages, select the worthy and enlightened to serve the altars of soil and grain, and the affairs of the realm will be settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Take his weapons and armor to equip the troops under your command, have Lu Youzhi lead them as vanguard, and your servant, within the Masters of Writing, will himself lead the hundred officials according to the precedents of former ages, select the worthy and enlightened to serve the altars of soil and grain, and the affairs of the realm will be settled at once.

sentences.zh: 又，朝廷諸所施為，民間傳言公悉豫之。

translations.literal: Moreover, among all the court's actions, popular rumor says Your Lordship had a hand in them all.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among all the court's actions, popular rumor says Your Lordship had a hand in them all.

sentences.zh: 公今不決，當有先公起事者，公亦不免附從之禍。

translations.literal: If Your Lordship does not decide now, someone will rise up before you—and you too will not escape the disaster of being dragged along in compliance.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Lordship does not decide now, someone will rise up before you—and you too will not escape the disaster of being dragged along in compliance.

sentences.zh: 聞車駕屢幸貴第，酣醉淹留；

translations.literal: I hear the imperial carriage repeatedly visits your noble residence and stays long in drunken revelry;
translations.idiomatic: I hear the imperial carriage repeatedly visits your noble residence and stays long in drunken revelry;

sentences.zh: 又聞屏左右，獨入閣內；

translations.literal: I also hear he dismisses his attendants and enters the pavilion alone—
translations.idiomatic: I also hear he dismisses his attendants and enters the pavilion alone—

sentences.zh: 此萬世一時，不可失也！」

translations.literal: this is the chance of ten thousand generations—it must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: this is the chance of ten thousand generations—it must not be lost!"

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「感君至言。

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "I am moved by your utmost words.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said, "I am moved by your utmost words.

sentences.zh: 然此大事，非僕所能行；

translations.literal: Yet this great affair is not something your servant can undertake;
translations.idiomatic: Yet this great affair is not something your servant can undertake;

sentences.zh: 事至，固當抱忠以沒耳。」

translations.literal: when the moment comes, I shall surely embrace loyalty and perish with it."
translations.idiomatic: when the moment comes, I shall surely embrace loyalty and perish with it."

sentences.zh: 青州刺史沈文秀，慶之弟子也，將之鎮，帥部曲出屯白下，亦說慶之曰：「主上狂暴如此，禍亂不久，而一門受其寵任，萬物皆謂與之同心。

translations.literal: The Governor of Qing province, Shen Wenxiu—a nephew-disciple of Qingzhi—was about to go to his post; leading his retainers he encamped at Baixia, and also urged Qingzhi, saying: "The ruler is so violent and ruthless; calamity and disorder will come before long. Yet our entire clan enjoys his favor and trust, and all the world thinks we share his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Qing province Shen Wenxiu, a nephew-disciple of Qingzhi, was about to take up his post; leading his personal troops he encamped at Baixia, and also urged Qingzhi, saying, "The emperor is so violent and ruthless; calamity and disorder will come before long. Yet our entire clan enjoys his favor and trust, and everyone believes we are of one mind with him.

sentences.zh: 且若人愛憎無常，猜忍特甚，不測之禍，進退難免。

translations.literal: Moreover, that man's likes and hates are inconstant; he is extraordinarily suspicious and cruel. Unforeseen disaster—whether advancing or retreating, one cannot escape it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his likes and hates are inconstant, and he is extraordinarily suspicious and cruel. Unforeseen disaster awaits; whether one advances or retreats, there is no escape.

sentences.zh: 今因此眾力，圖之易於反掌。

translations.literal: Now, using this host of force, to plot against him would be easier than turning one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: With this force at hand, removing him would be as easy as turning one's hand.

sentences.zh: 機會難值，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Such an opportunity is hard to meet—it must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Such a chance comes rarely and must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 再三言之，至於流涕，慶之終不從。

translations.literal: He spoke thus again and again, even to the point of weeping; Qingzhi in the end would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated this again and again, even to the point of tears; Qingzhi still refused.

sentences.zh: 文秀遂行。

translations.literal: Wenxiu thereupon departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu then set out on his journey.

sentences.zh: 及帝誅何邁，量慶之必當入諫，先閉青溪諸橋以絕之。

translations.literal: When the emperor executed He Mai, he calculated that Qingzhi would surely enter to remonstrate, and beforehand closed all the bridges over the Qing Stream to cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qianfei executed He Mai, he calculated that Qingzhi would surely come to remonstrate, and beforehand closed all the bridges over the Qing Stream to block him.

sentences.zh: 慶之聞之，果往，不得進而還。

translations.literal: Qingzhi heard of it, went as expected, could not advance, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi heard of this, went as expected, could not get through, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 帝乃使慶之從父兄子直閣將軍攸之賜慶之藥。

translations.literal: The emperor then had Youzhi, Qingzhi's first cousin once removed and a Direct-Palace General, present Qingzhi with poison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Qingzhi's first cousin, Direct-Palace General Youzhi, send poison to Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 慶之不肯飲，攸之以被掩殺之，時年八十。

translations.literal: Qingzhi refused to drink; Youzhi smothered him with a quilt and killed him. He was then eighty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi refused to drink; Youzhi smothered him with a quilt and killed him. He was eighty years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 慶之子侍中文叔欲亡。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's son, Attendant-in-ordinary Wenshu, wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi's son, Attendant-in-ordinary Wenshu, wished to flee.

sentences.zh: 恐如太宰義恭被支解，謂其弟中書郎文季曰：「我能死，爾能報。」

translations.literal: Fearing he would suffer dismemberment like Grand Tutor Yigong, he said to his younger brother, Secretariat Gentleman Wenji: "I can die; you can avenge."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be dismembered like Grand Tutor Yigong, he said to his younger brother, Secretariat Gentleman Wenji, "I can die; you can avenge us."

sentences.zh: 遂飲慶之之藥而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drank the poison sent to Qingzhi and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then drank the poison sent for Qingzhi and died.

sentences.zh: 弟秘書郎昭明亦自經死。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Secretariat Secretary Zhaoming, also hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother, Secretariat Secretary Zhaoming, also hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 文季揮刀馳馬而去。

translations.literal: Wenji waved a blade, mounted a horse, and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji drew a blade, mounted a horse, and galloped away.

sentences.zh: 追者不敢逼，遂得免。

translations.literal: Pursuers did not dare press close, and he thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His pursuers did not dare close in, and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 帝詐言慶之病薨，贈侍中、太尉，謚曰忠武公，葬禮甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor falsely announced that Qingzhi had died of illness; he was posthumously given attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Commandant, honored with the posthumous title Duke Loyal and Martial, and buried with great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor falsely announced that Qingzhi had died of illness; he was posthumously made attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Commandant, given the posthumous title Duke Loyal and Martial, and buried with great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍王玄謨數流涕諫帝以刑殺過差，帝大怒。

translations.literal: Army Inspector General Wang Xuanmo repeatedly remonstrated with tears that the emperor's executions and killings were excessive; the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Army Inspector General Wang Xuanmo repeatedly remonstrated in tears that the emperor's executions were excessive; the emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 玄謨宿將，有威名，道路訛言玄謨已見誅。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was an old general of established repute; on the roads false rumor spread that Xuanmo had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was a veteran commander of established reputation, and false rumors spread along the roads that he had already been executed.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗嘗為東陽太守，玄謨典簽包法榮家在東陽，玄謨使法榮至興宗所。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong had once been Administrator of Dongyang; Xuanmo's chief clerk Bao Farong's family was in Dongyang, and Xuanmo sent Farong to Xingzong's place.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong had once been Administrator of Dongyang; Xuanmo's chief clerk Bao Farong was from Dongyang, and Xuanmo sent Farong to see Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 興宗謂法榮曰：「領軍殊當憂懼。」

translations.literal: Xingzong said to Farong: "The Army Inspector must be in extreme worry and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said to Farong, "The Army Inspector must be deeply worried and afraid."

sentences.zh: 法榮曰：「領軍比日殆不復食，夜亦不眠，恆言收己在門，不保俄頃。」

translations.literal: Farong said: "The Army Inspector these past days has hardly eaten at all; by night he does not sleep, constantly saying that arrest is already at the door and that he cannot guarantee even a moment's safety."
translations.idiomatic: Farong said, "The Army Inspector these past days has barely eaten; he does not sleep at night and keeps saying that arrest is at the door and that he cannot count on surviving another moment."

sentences.zh: 興宗曰：「領軍憂懼，當為方略，那得坐待禍至！」

translations.literal: Xingzong said: "If the Army Inspector worries and fears, he should devise a plan—how can he sit and wait for disaster to arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong said, "If the Army Inspector is afraid, he ought to devise a plan—how can he sit and wait for disaster!"

sentences.zh: 因使法榮勸玄謨舉事。

translations.literal: He thereupon had Farong urge Xuanmo to rise in arms.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Farong urge Xuanmo to rise up.

sentences.zh: 玄謨使法榮謝曰：「此亦未易可行，期當不洩君言。」

translations.literal: Xuanmo had Farong decline, saying: "This too is not easily doable; I promise not to reveal your words."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo had Farong decline, saying, "That too is not easily done; I promise not to reveal what you said."

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍劉道隆，為帝所寵任，專典禁兵。

translations.literal: Right Guard General Liu Daolong was favored and trusted by the emperor and exclusively managed the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Liu Daolong was favored and trusted by the emperor and held sole charge of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 興宗嘗與之俱從帝夜出，道隆過興宗車後，興宗曰：「劉君！

translations.literal: Xingzong once went out at night with the emperor together with him; Daolong passed behind Xingzong's carriage, and Xingzong said: "Master Liu!
translations.idiomatic: Xingzong once went out at night with the emperor in Daolong's company; as Daolong passed behind Xingzong's carriage, Xingzong said, "Master Liu!

sentences.zh: 比日思一閒寫。」

translations.literal: These past days I have been wanting a quiet talk."
translations.idiomatic: These days I've been wanting a quiet talk."

sentences.zh: 道隆解其意，掐興宗手曰：「蔡公勿多言！」

translations.literal: Daolong understood his meaning, squeezed Xingzong's hand, and said: "Master Cai, speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Daolong understood his meaning, squeezed Xingzong's hand, and said, "Master Cai, say no more!"

sentences.zh: 壬寅，立皇后路氏，太皇太后弟道慶之女也。

translations.literal: On renyin, Empress Lady Lu was installed—daughter of Daqing, younger brother of the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Lady Lu was installed as empress; she was the daughter of Daqing, younger brother of the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝畏忌諸父，恐其在外為患，皆聚之建康，拘於殿內，毆捶陵曳，無復人理。

translations.literal: The emperor feared and resented his uncles, fearing they would cause trouble outside; he gathered them all at Jiankang, confined them within the palace halls, beating, flogging, and humiliating them until no human decency remained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared his uncles and worried they would cause trouble if left outside the capital; he gathered them all at Jiankang, confined them inside the palace halls, and beat, flogged, and humiliated them with no regard for human decency.

sentences.zh: 湘東王彧、建安王休仁、山陽王休祐，皆肥壯，帝為竹籠，盛而稱之，以彧尤肥，謂之「豬王」，謂休仁為「殺王」，休祐為「賊王」。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong Yu, the Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, and the Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were all stout and robust; the emperor made bamboo cages, placed them inside, and weighed them. Because Yu was especially fat, he called him "Pig King"; he called Xiuren "Slaughter King" and Xiuyou "Bandit King."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Yu, Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, and Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou were all stout and robust; the emperor made bamboo cages, placed them inside, and weighed them. Because Yu was especially fat, he called him "Pig King"; Xiuren he called "Slaughter King," and Xiuyou "Bandit King."

sentences.zh: 以三王年長，尤惡之，常錄以自隨，不離左右。

translations.literal: Because the three princes were older, he especially hated them and constantly kept them at his side, never leaving them from his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Because the three princes were older, he especially hated them and kept them constantly at his side, never letting them leave.

sentences.zh: 東海王禕性凡劣，謂之「驢王」；

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai Yi was coarse and inferior in character; he called him "Donkey King";
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Donghai Yi was dull and coarse in character; the emperor called him "Donkey King";

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休范、巴陵王休若年尚少，故並得從容。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guiyang Xiufan and the Prince of Baling Xiuruo were still young, and so both could live at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guiyang Xiufan and Prince of Baling Xiuruo were still young, and so both were left relatively unmolested.

sentences.zh: 嘗以木槽盛飯，並雜食攪之，掘地為坑，實以泥水，裸彧內坑中，使以口就槽食之，用為歡笑。

translations.literal: He once filled a wooden trough with food, mixed in assorted scraps, dug a pit in the ground and filled it with mud and water, stripped Yu naked and put him in the pit, and made him eat from the trough with his mouth—they took this for mirth.
translations.idiomatic: He once filled a wooden trough with food mixed with refuse, dug a pit filled with mud and water, stripped Yu naked and placed him in it, and made him eat from the trough with his mouth—all for amusement.

sentences.zh: 前後欲殺三王以十數；

translations.literal: Before and after, he wished to kill the three princes on more than ten occasions;
translations.idiomatic: On more than ten occasions he tried to have the three princes killed;

sentences.zh: 休仁多智數，每以談笑佞諛說之，故得推遷。

translations.literal: Xiuren was clever and resourceful; each time he used jesting flattery to talk him out of it, and so the matter was repeatedly postponed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren was clever and resourceful; each time he used jest and flattery to talk him out of it, and so execution was repeatedly postponed.

sentences.zh: 少府劉曚妾孕臨月，帝迎入後宮，俟其生男，欲立為太子。

translations.literal: Steward Liu Meng's concubine was pregnant and near term; the emperor welcomed her into the inner palace, waiting for her to bear a son whom he wished to install as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Steward Liu Meng's concubine was pregnant and near full term; the emperor brought her into the inner palace, planning to install her son as crown prince if she bore a boy.

sentences.zh: 彧嘗忤旨，帝裸之，縛其手足，貫之以杖，使人提付太官，曰：「今日屠豬！」

translations.literal: Yu once offended the imperial will; the emperor stripped him naked, bound his hands and feet, threaded a pole through them, had men carry him off to the Imperial Kitchen, and said: "Today we slaughter the pig!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu once offended the emperor; he stripped him naked, bound his hands and feet, ran a pole through them, had men carry him to the Imperial Kitchen, and said, "Today we slaughter the pig!"

sentences.zh: 休仁笑曰：「豬未應死。」

translations.literal: Xiuren smiled and said: "The pig should not die yet."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren smiled and said, "The pig shouldn't die yet."

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，休仁曰：「待皇太子生，殺豬取其肝肺。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked why; Xiuren said: "Wait until the crown prince is born, then slaughter the pig and take its liver and lungs."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, Xiuren said, "Wait until the crown prince is born, then slaughter the pig for his liver and lungs."

sentences.zh: 帝怒乃解，曰：「且付廷尉。」

translations.literal: The emperor's anger subsided and he released him, saying: "For now, hand him over to the Minister of Justice."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger cooled and he relented, saying, "For now, hand him over to the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 一宿，釋之。

translations.literal: After one night, he released him.
translations.idiomatic: After one night, he set him free.

sentences.zh: 丁未，曚妾生子，名曰皇子，為之大赦，賜為父後者爵一級。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Meng's concubine bore a son; he was named Imperial Son; a general amnesty was proclaimed, and those who became heirs to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Meng's concubine bore a son, named Imperial Son; the emperor proclaimed a general amnesty and granted one rank of nobility to those who became heirs to their fathers.

sentences.zh: 帝又以太祖、世祖在兄弟數皆第三，江州刺史晉安王子勳亦第三，故惡之，因何邁之謀，使左右朱景雲送藥賜子勳死。

translations.literal: The emperor also noted that Taizu and Shizu were both third among brothers in birth order, and Zixun, Prince of Jin'an and Governor of Jiang province, was also third—therefore he hated him. Following He Mai's plot, he sent his attendant Zhu Jingyun with poison to command Zixun's death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also noted that Emperor Wen and Emperor Xiaowu had both been third among their brothers, and that Zixun, Prince of Jin'an and Governor of Jiang province, was also third—so he hated him. Following He Mai's scheme, he sent his attendant Zhu Jingyun with poison to command Zixun's death.

sentences.zh: 景雲至湓口，停不進。

translations.literal: Jingyun reached Penkou and halted, not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun reached Penkou and stopped, refusing to go farther.

sentences.zh: 子勳典簽謝道邁、主帥潘欣之、侍書褚靈嗣聞之，馳以告長史鄧琬，泣涕請計。

translations.literal: Zixun's chief clerk Xie Daomai, chief commander Pan Xinzhi, and attendant scribe Chu Lingsi heard of it; they galloped to inform Chief Administrator Deng Wan, weeping and begging for a plan.
