translations.idiomatic: Zixun's chief clerk Xie Daomai, chief commander Pan Xinzhi, and attendant scribe Chu Lingsi heard of it; they galloped to tell Chief Administrator Deng Wan, weeping and begging for a plan.

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「身南土寒士，蒙先帝殊恩，以愛子見托，豈得惜門戶百口，期當以死報效。

translations.literal: Wan said: "I am a humble scholar of the southern lands, who received the late emperor's extraordinary grace in being entrusted with his beloved son—how could I spare the hundred mouths of my clan? I expect to repay this with my death.
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "I am a humble scholar from the south who received the late emperor's extraordinary grace when he entrusted his beloved son to me—how could I spare the lives of my entire clan? I mean to repay that trust with my death.

sentences.zh: 幼主昏暴，社稷危殆，雖曰天子，事猶獨夫。

translations.literal: The young ruler is benighted and violent; the altars of soil and grain are in peril. Though called Son of Heaven, in deed he is but a lone tyrant.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor is benighted and brutal; the realm is in peril. Though he is called Son of Heaven, in truth he is nothing but a tyrant.

sentences.zh: 今便指帥文武，直造京邑，與群公卿士，廢昏立明耳。」

translations.literal: Now let us immediately lead civil and military officials straight to the capital, and together with the lords, ministers, and grandees, depose the benighted and establish the enlightened—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Let us now lead our civil and military officials straight to the capital and, together with the lords and ministers, depose the benighted ruler and install a wise one—that is all there is to it."

sentences.zh: 戊申，琬稱子勳教，令所部戒嚴。

translations.literal: On wushen, Wan issued orders in Zixun's name, commanding his subordinates to stand at alert.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Wan issued orders in Zixun's name commanding his forces to mobilize.

sentences.zh: 子勳戎服出聽事，集僚佐，使潘欣之口宣旨諭之。

translations.literal: Zixun came out to the reception hall in martial dress, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi orally proclaim the edict and explain it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun appeared at court in armor, assembled his staff, and had Pan Xinzhi proclaim the edict to them.

sentences.zh: 四座未對，錄事參軍陶亮首請效死前驅，眾皆奉旨。

translations.literal: Before the assembly could respond, Recording General Tao Liang was first to request to die as vanguard; all accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Before anyone else could speak, Recording General Tao Liang was the first to offer to die in the vanguard; all accepted the command.

sentences.zh: 乃以亮為咨議參軍，領中兵，總統軍事；

translations.literal: Liang was then made Advisory General, commanding central troops and overseeing all military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Liang was made Advisory General, placed in command of the central troops, and given overall military authority;

sentences.zh: 功曹張沈為咨議參軍，統作舟艦；

translations.literal: Clerk Zhang Shen was made Advisory General, overseeing the building of warships;
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhang Shen was made Advisory General and put in charge of building warships;

sentences.zh: 南陽太守沈懷寶、岷山太守薛常寶、彭澤令陳紹宗等並為將帥。

translations.literal: Administrator of Nanyang Shen Huaibao, Administrator of Minshan Xue Changbao, Magistrate of Pengze Chen Shaozong, and others were all made generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator of Nanyang Shen Huaibao, Administrator of Minshan Xue Changbao, Magistrate of Pengze Chen Shaozong, and others were all appointed as commanders.

sentences.zh: 初，帝使荊州錄送前軍長史、荊州行事張悅至湓口，琬稱子勳命，釋其桎梏，迎以所乘車，以為司馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had Jing province escort under guard the former Forward Army Chief Administrator and acting Jing provincial director Zhang Yue to Penkou. Wan, invoking Zixun's command, released him from fetters, welcomed him with his own carriage, and made him Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had had Jing province escort under guard Forward Army Chief Administrator and acting Jing provincial director Zhang Yue to Penkou. Wan, invoking Zixun's authority, freed him from his shackles, welcomed him in his own carriage, and made him Chief Administrator.

sentences.zh: 悅，暢之弟也。

translations.literal: Yue was the younger brother of Changzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was Changzhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 琬、悅二人共掌內外眾事，遣將軍俞伯奇帥五百人斷大雷，禁絕商旅及公私使命。

translations.literal: Wan and Yue together managed all matters internal and external; they sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to block Dalei, forbidding merchants, travelers, and public and private envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and Yue together managed all internal and external affairs; they sent General Yu Boqi with five hundred men to block Dalei, cutting off merchants, travelers, and all public and private envoys.

sentences.zh: 遣使上諸郡民丁，收斂器械；

translations.literal: They sent envoys to the commanderies to call up civilian levies and gather weapons;
translations.idiomatic: They sent envoys to the commanderies to call up civilian levies and gather weapons;

sentences.zh: 旬日之內，得甲士五千人，出頓大雷，於兩岸築壘。

translations.literal: Within ten days they mustered five thousand armored soldiers, encamped at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days they mustered five thousand armored soldiers, encamped at Dalei, and built fortifications on both banks of the river.

sentences.zh: 又以巴東、建平二郡太守孫沖之為咨議參軍，領中兵，與陶亮並統前軍，移檄遠近。

translations.literal: Sun Chongzhi, Administrator of both Badong and Jianping commanderies, was additionally made Advisory General commanding central troops; he and Tao Liang jointly commanded the vanguard, and a proclamation was sent far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chongzhi, Administrator of Badong and Jianping commanderies, was made Advisory General and placed in command of the central troops; he and Tao Liang jointly led the vanguard, and proclamations were sent far and wide.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝召諸妃、主列於前，強左右使辱之。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the emperor summoned the various princesses consorts and princesses and lined them up before him, forcing his attendants to humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the emperor summoned the imperial consorts and princesses and lined them up before him, forcing his attendants to humiliate them.

sentences.zh: 南平王鑠妃江氏不從；

translations.literal: The consort of the Prince of Nanping Shuo, Lady Jiang, refused;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang, consort of Prince of Nanping Shuo, refused;

sentences.zh: 帝怒，殺妃三子南平王敬猷、廬陵王敬先、安南侯敬淵，鞭江妃一百。

translations.literal: The emperor was angered; he killed the consort's three sons—Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan—and flogged Lady Jiang one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; he killed her three sons—Prince of Nanping Jingyou, Prince of Luling Jingxian, and Marquis of Annan Jingyuan—and flogged Lady Jiang one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 先是民間訛言湘中出天子，帝將南巡荊、湘二州以厭之。

translations.literal: Earlier, popular rumor said a Son of Heaven would arise in Xiangzhong; the emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang provinces to suppress the omen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, rumor spread that a Son of Heaven would arise in the Xiang region; the emperor planned a southern tour of Jing and Xiang provinces to dispel the omen.

sentences.zh: 明旦，欲先誅湘東王彧，然後發。

translations.literal: The next morning he intended first to execute the Prince of Xiangdong Yu, and then set out.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he planned first to execute Prince of Xiangdong Yu, then set out on his tour.

sentences.zh: 初，帝既殺諸公，恐群下謀己，以直閣將軍宗越、譚金、童太一、沈攸之等有勇力，引為爪牙，賞賜美人、金帛，充牣其家。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the emperor had killed the princes, he feared his subordinates would plot against him; because Direct-Palace Generals Zong Yue, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and Shen Youzhi had courage and strength, he drew them in as claws and fangs, bestowing beauties, gold, and silk until their homes overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had killed the princes, he feared his subordinates would plot against him; because Direct-Palace Generals Zong Yue, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and Shen Youzhi were men of courage and strength, he enlisted them as his enforcers, lavishing them with beauties, gold, and silk until their homes overflowed.

sentences.zh: 趙等久在殿省，眾所畏服，皆為帝盡力；

translations.literal: Yue and the others had long served in the palace offices; all feared and submitted to them, and all exerted themselves for the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Yue and the others had long served in the palace; everyone feared them, and they all served the emperor zealously;

sentences.zh: 帝恃之，益無所顧憚，恣為不道，中外騷然。

translations.literal: The emperor relied on them and grew ever more without restraint, acting wantonly against the Way; court and countryside were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on them, the emperor grew ever bolder, behaving with lawless abandon; the court and countryside were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 左右宿衛之士皆有異志，而畏越等，不敢發。

translations.literal: The palace guards on left and right all harbored divergent intents, yet feared Yue and the others and dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards all harbored rebellious thoughts, but feared Yue and the others and dared not move.

sentences.zh: 時三王久幽，不知所為，湘東王彧主衣會稽阮佃夫、內監吳興王道隆、學官令臨淮李道兒與直閣將軍柳光世，及帝左右琅邪淳於文祖等陰謀弒帝。

translations.literal: At this time the three princes had long been confined and knew not what to do. The Prince of Xiangdong Yu's Master of Robes Ruan Tianfu of Kuaiji, Inner Supervisor Wang Daolong of Wuxing, Director of Studies Li Dao'er of Linhuai, Direct-Palace General Liu Guangshi, and the emperor's attendant Chunyu Wenzu of Langya secretly plotted to assassinate the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the three princes had long been imprisoned and knew not what to do. Prince of Xiangdong Yu's Master of Robes Ruan Tianfu, Inner Supervisor Wang Daolong, Director of Studies Li Dao'er, Direct-Palace General Liu Guangshi, and the emperor's attendant Chunyu Wenzu of Langya secretly plotted to assassinate the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以立後故，假諸王閹人。

translations.literal: Because of the empress's installation, the emperor temporarily assigned eunuchs to the various princes.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empress had just been installed, the emperor temporarily assigned eunuchs to the various princes.

sentences.zh: 彧左右錢藍生亦在中，彧密使候帝動止。

translations.literal: Yu's attendant Qian Lansheng was also among them; Yu secretly had him watch the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's attendant Qian Lansheng was among them, and Yu secretly had him watch the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝游華林園竹林堂，使宮人裸相逐，一人不從命，斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor toured the Bamboo Grove Hall in Hualin Park, made palace women chase one another naked; one who did not obey was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while touring the Bamboo Grove Hall in Hualin Park, the emperor made palace women chase one another naked; one who refused was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 夜，夢在竹林堂，有女子罵曰：「帝悖虐不道，明年不及熟矣！」

translations.literal: By night he dreamed he was in the Bamboo Grove Hall; a woman cursed, saying: "The emperor is perverse, cruel, and against the Way—next year the grain will not ripen!"
translations.idiomatic: That night he dreamed he was in the Bamboo Grove Hall; a woman cursed him, saying, "The emperor is perverse and cruel—next year you won't live to see the harvest ripen!"

sentences.zh: 帝於宮中求得一人似所夢者斬之。

translations.literal: In the palace he found a woman resembling the one in the dream and beheaded her.
translations.idiomatic: He found a woman in the palace who resembled the one in his dream and had her beheaded.

sentences.zh: 又夢所殺者罵曰：「我已訴上帝矣！」

translations.literal: Again he dreamed the woman he had killed cursed, saying: "I have already appealed to the Supreme Lord on High!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he dreamed that the woman he had killed cursed him, saying, "I have already appealed to Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 於是巫覡言竹林堂有鬼。

translations.literal: Thereupon the shamans and diviners said the Bamboo Grove Hall had a ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Then the shamans declared that the Bamboo Grove Hall was haunted.

sentences.zh: 是日晡時，帝出華林園。

translations.literal: That day at the hour of shen, the emperor left Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: That afternoon the emperor left Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁、山陽王休祐、會稽公主並從，湘東王彧獨在秘書省，不被召，益憂懼。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, the Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, and the Princess of Kuaiji all followed; the Prince of Xiangdong Yu alone remained at the Secretariat—he was not summoned—and grew ever more worried and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren, Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, and the Princess of Kuaiji all accompanied him; Prince of Xiangdong Yu alone remained at the Secretariat, not summoned, and grew ever more fearful.

sentences.zh: 帝素惡主衣吳興壽寂之，見輒切齒，阮佃夫以其謀告寂之及外監典事東陽朱幼、細鎧主南彭城姜產之、細鎧將晉陵王敬則、中書舍人戴明寶。

translations.literal: The emperor had long hated Yu's Master of Robes Shou Jizhi of Wuxing and gnashed his teeth at the sight of him. Ruan Tianfu told Jizhi and the others of the plot—Outer Supervisor Director Zhu You of Dongyang, Fine-Armour Commander Jiang Chanzhi of Nan Pengcheng, Fine-Armour General Wang Jingze of Jinling, and Secretariat Cadet Dai Mingbao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long hated Master of Robes Shou Jizhi and gnashed his teeth whenever he saw him. Ruan Tianfu confided the plot to Jizhi, Outer Supervisor Director Zhu You, Fine-Armour Commander Jiang Chanzhi, Fine-Armour General Wang Jingze, and Secretariat Cadet Dai Mingbao.

sentences.zh: 寂之等聞之，皆響應。

translations.literal: When Jizhi and the others heard of it, all responded in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi and the others all agreed to join.

sentences.zh: 幼豫約勒內外，使錢藍生密報休仁、休祐。

translations.literal: You arranged and bound matters inside and outside, and had Qian Lansheng secretly inform Xiuren and Xiuyou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu You coordinated matters inside and outside the palace, and had Qian Lansheng secretly warn Xiuren and Xiuyou.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲南巡，腹心宗越等並聽出外裝束，唯隊主樊僧整防華林閣。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor wished to tour south; his inner confidants Zong Yue and the rest were all permitted to go out to prepare, and only Squad Commander Fan Sengzheng guarded the Hualin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing for his southern tour; his trusted henchmen Zong Yue and the rest had all been sent out to prepare, and only Squad Commander Fan Sengzheng remained guarding the Hualin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 柳光世與僧整，鄉人，因密邀之；

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi and Sengzheng were fellow townsmen; he therefore secretly invited him;
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi and Sengzheng were from the same hometown; Guangshi secretly recruited him;

sentences.zh: 僧整即受命。

translations.literal: Sengzheng immediately accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Sengzheng agreed at once.

sentences.zh: 凡同謀十餘人。

translations.literal: In all, more than ten men shared the plot.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten men in all joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫慮力少不濟，更欲招合，壽寂之曰：「謀廣或洩，不煩多人。」

translations.literal: Ruan Tianfu worried that their force was too small to succeed and wished to recruit more; Shou Jizhi said: "If the plot grows broad it may leak—there is no need for many men."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tianfu worried their force was too small and wanted to recruit more men; Shou Jizhi said, "The wider the plot, the more likely it leaks—there's no need for a crowd."

sentences.zh: 其夕，帝悉屏侍衛，與群巫及綵女數百人射鬼於竹林堂。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor dismissed all his guards and, with a crowd of shamans and hundreds of maidens in colored dress, shot at ghosts in the Bamboo Grove Hall.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the emperor dismissed all his guards and, with shamans and hundreds of maidens, shot at ghosts in the Bamboo Grove Hall.

sentences.zh: 事畢，將奏樂，壽寂之抽刀前入，姜產之次之，淳於文祖等皆隨其後。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished and music was about to be played, Jizhi drew his blade and advanced; Jiang Chanzhi came next; Chunyu Wenzu and the rest all followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: When it was over and the musicians were about to play, Jizhi drew his blade and rushed in, Jiang Chanzhi right behind him, with Chunyu Wenzu and the others following.

sentences.zh: 休仁聞行聲甚疾，謂休祐曰：「事作矣！」

translations.literal: Xiuren heard footsteps very rapid and said to Xiuyou: "It has begun!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren heard rapid footsteps and said to Xiuyou, "It's begun!"

sentences.zh: 相隨奔景陽山。

translations.literal: They fled together toward Jingyang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: They fled together toward Jingyang Hill.

sentences.zh: 帝山寂之至，引弓射之，不中。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Jizhi arrive, drew his bow, and shot at him but missed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor saw Jizhi coming, he drew his bow and shot at him but missed.

sentences.zh: 綵女皆迸走。

translations.literal: The maidens in colored dress all fled scattering.
translations.idiomatic: The maidens all fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 帝亦走，大呼「寂寂」者三。

translations.literal: The emperor also fled, crying out "Jiji!" three times.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also fled, shouting "Jizhi! Jizhi! Jizhi!" three times.

sentences.zh: 寂之追而弒之；

translations.literal: Jizhi pursued and assassinated him;
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi pursued him and killed him;

sentences.zh: 宣令宿衛曰：「湘東王受太皇太后令，除征主，今已平定。」

translations.literal: An edict was proclaimed to the night guards, saying: "The Prince of Xiangdong Yu has received the Grand Empress Dowager's order to remove the tyrant, and has now brought the matter to settlement."
translations.idiomatic: Orders were announced to the night guards: "Prince of Xiangdong Yu has received the Grand Empress Dowager's command to remove the tyrant, and the disturbance is now settled."

sentences.zh: 殿省惶惑，未知所為。

translations.literal: The palace halls and offices were alarmed and confused, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The palace halls and offices were panicked and uncertain what to do.

sentences.zh: 休仁就秘書省見湘東王，即稱臣，引升西堂，登御座，召見諸大臣。

translations.literal: Xiuren went to the Secretariat to see the Prince of Xiangdong Yu, at once called himself his subject, led him up to the Western Hall, ascended the imperial seat, and summoned the various ministers to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren went to the Secretariat to see Prince of Xiangdong Yu, immediately declared himself his subject, led him to the Western Hall, seated him on the imperial throne, and summoned the ministers.

sentences.zh: 於時事起倉猝，王失履，跣至西堂，猶著烏帽。

translations.literal: At that time the affair had risen in sudden haste; the prince had lost his shoes and came barefoot to the Western Hall, still wearing a black cap.
translations.idiomatic: Events had erupted so suddenly that the prince had lost his shoes and arrived barefoot at the Western Hall, still in a black cap.

sentences.zh: 坐定，休仁呼主衣以白帽代之。

translations.literal: When he was seated, Xiuren summoned the Master of Robes to replace it with a white cap.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was seated, Xiuren called for the Master of Robes to exchange it for a white cap.

sentences.zh: 令備羽儀，雖未即位，凡事悉稱令書施行。

translations.literal: He ordered the insignia of office prepared; though he had not yet taken the throne, all matters were at once issued and carried out in the name of commands.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the imperial regalia prepared; though he had not yet been enthroned, all affairs were issued and executed as written commands.

sentences.zh: 宣太皇太后令，數廢帝罪惡，命湘東王纂承皇極。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager's order was proclaimed, recounting the Deposed Emperor's crimes and wickedness, and commanding the Prince of Xiangdong Yu to succeed to the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager's edict was proclaimed, listing Emperor Qianfei's crimes, and Prince of Xiangdong Yu was commanded to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 及時，宗越等始入，湘東王撫接甚厚。

translations.literal: By this time, Zong Yue and the others finally entered, and the Prince of Xiangdong Yu treated them with great kindness and welcome.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zong Yue and the others finally arrived, and Prince of Xiangdong Yu received them with marked warmth.

sentences.zh: 廢帝母弟司徒、揚州刺史、豫章王子尚，頑悖有兄風，己未，湘東王以太皇太后令，賜子尚及會稽公主死。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor's younger brother by the same mother—the Minister over the Masses, Governor of Yang province, and Prince of Yuzhang Zishang—was stubborn and rebellious and had his elder brother's temperament. On jiwei, the Prince of Xiangdong Yu, by the Grand Empress Dowager's order, granted Zishang and the Princess of Kuaiji death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei's younger brother, Minister over the Masses and Governor of Yang province Prince of Yuzhang Zishang, was as vicious and rebellious as his brother. On jiwei, by the Grand Empress Dowager's order, Prince of Xiangdong Yu condemned Zishang and the Princess of Kuaiji to death.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁等始得出居外捨。

translations.literal: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and the others were finally able to go out and reside in outer quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jian'an Xiuren and the others were finally allowed to leave and take up quarters outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 釋謝莊之囚。

translations.literal: The prisoner Xie Zhuang was released.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhuang was released from prison.

sentences.zh: 廢帝猶橫屍太醫閣口。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor's corpse still lay stretched across the entrance to the Imperial Medical Office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianfei's body still lay in the doorway of the Imperial Medical Office.

sentences.zh: 蔡興宗謂尚書右僕射王彧曰：「此雖凶悖，要是天下之主，宜使喪禮粗足；

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong said to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu: "Though this man was vicious and rebellious, he was after all ruler of all under Heaven; the funeral rites ought at least to be roughly adequate;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong said to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu, "Vicious as he was, he was nevertheless the sovereign of the realm; the funeral should at least meet the bare minimum of ritual;

sentences.zh: 若直如此，四海必將乘人。」

translations.literal: If it is left just like this, all within the four seas will surely take advantage of men's weakness."
translations.idiomatic: If he is simply left like this, the whole empire will seize upon it to its advantage."

sentences.zh: 乃葬之秣陵縣南。

translations.literal: He was therefore buried south of Moling county.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried south of Moling county.

sentences.zh: 初，湘東王母沈婕妤早卒，路太后養之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Xiangdong Yu's mother, Lady Shen the Beautiful Talisman, had died early, and Empress Dowager Lu had raised him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangdong Yu's mother, Lady Shen, had died early, and Empress Dowager Lu had raised him.

sentences.zh: 王事太后甚謹，太后愛王亦篤。

translations.literal: The prince served the empress dowager with great diligence, and the empress dowager also loved the prince deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He had served the empress dowager devotedly, and she had loved him in return.

sentences.zh: 王既弒廢帝，欲慰太后心，下令以太后弟子休之為黃門侍郎，茂之為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Since the prince had assassinated the Deposed Emperor and wished to console the empress dowager's heart, he issued an order appointing the empress dowager's younger clansmen Xiuzhi as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Maozhi as Gentleman Attendant at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Emperor Qianfei, he wished to reassure the empress dowager and appointed her clansmen Xiuzhi and Maozhi as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Gentleman Attendant at the Secretariat, respectively.

sentences.zh: 論功行賞，壽寂之等十四人皆封縣侯、縣子。

translations.literal: Merit was assessed and rewards conferred; Shou Jizhi and the other fourteen men were all enfeoffed as marquises of counties and viscounts of counties.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were distributed for merit; Shou Jizhi and thirteen others were all enfeoffed as county marquises or county viscounts.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚申朔，以東海王禕為中書監、太尉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the gengshen new moon, Prince of Donghai Yi was made Director of the Secretariat and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the gengshen new moon, Prince of Donghai Yi was appointed Director of the Secretariat and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 進鎮軍將軍、江州刺史晉安王子勳為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: General Who Stabilizes the Army and Governor of Jiang province Prince of Jin'an Zixun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commissioner Equal to the Three Excellencies with an Acting Staff.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Stabilizes the Army and Governor of Jiang province Prince of Jin'an Zixun was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with the privileges of the Three Excellencies and an acting staff.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以建安王休仁為司徒、尚書令、揚州刺史，以山陽王休祐為荊州刺史，桂陽王休范為南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On guihai, Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Minister over the Masses, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yang province; Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Governor of Jing province; and Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was made Governor of Southern Xu province.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Prince of Jian'an Xiuren was made Minister over the Masses, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yang province; Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was made Governor of Jing province; and Prince of Guiyang Xiufan was made Governor of Southern Xu province.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，徙安陸王子綏為江夏王。

translations.literal: On yichou, Prince of Anlu Zisui was transferred to be Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Prince of Anlu Zisui was reassigned as Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，湘東王即皇帝位，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Prince of Xiangdong Yu ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Prince of Xiangdong Yu took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 其廢帝時昏制謬封，並皆刊削。

translations.literal: The foolish statutes and mistaken enfeoffments of the Deposed Emperor's time were all struck out and pruned away.
translations.idiomatic: All the erratic laws and improper enfeoffments of Emperor Qianfei's reign were revoked.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以右衛將軍劉道隆為中護軍。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Right Guards General Liu Daolong was made General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, General of the Right Guards Liu Daolong was appointed General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 道隆暱於廢帝，嘗無禮於建安太妃；

translations.literal: Daolong had been intimate with the Deposed Emperor and had once been disrespectful to the Prince of Jian'an's consort;
translations.idiomatic: Daolong had been a favorite of Emperor Qianfei and had once insulted Prince of Jian'an's consort;

sentences.zh: 至是，建安王休仁求解職，明帝乃賜道隆死。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Jian'an Xiuren requested to resign his office, and Emperor Ming thereupon granted Daolong death.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren then requested to resign his post, and Emperor Ming had Daolong executed.

sentences.zh: 宗越、譚金、童太一等雖為上所撫接，內不自安；

translations.literal: Although Zong Yue, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and the others had been treated with kindness and welcome by the emperor, inwardly they were not at ease;
translations.idiomatic: Although Zong Yue, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and the others had been treated warmly by the emperor, they remained inwardly uneasy;

sentences.zh: 上亦不欲使居中，從容謂曰：「卿等遭罹暴朝，勤勞日久，應得自養之地；

translations.literal: The emperor also did not wish them to remain at court and, speaking at his ease, said to them: "You have suffered under the tyrannical court and toiled long; you ought to have places where you may retire and rest yourselves;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also did not want them at court and said gently, "You endured the tyrant's reign and have served long; you deserve provinces where you can rest and recuperate;

sentences.zh: 兵馬大郡，隨卿等所擇。」

translations.literal: Great commanderies with troops and horses—choose as you will."
translations.idiomatic: Choose whichever great military commanderies you prefer."

sentences.zh: 越等素已自疑，聞之，皆相顧失色，因謀作亂；

translations.literal: Yue and the others had long been suspicious of themselves; hearing this, they all looked at one another and lost color, and thereupon plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: They had already been suspicious; on hearing this, they exchanged frightened glances and plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 以告沈攸之，攸之以聞。

translations.literal: They told Shen Youzhi, and Youzhi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: They confided in Shen Youzhi, who reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 上收越等，下獄死。

translations.literal: The emperor arrested Yue and the others and had them imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Yue and his co-conspirators arrested, imprisoned, and executed.

sentences.zh: 攸之復入直閣。

translations.literal: Youzhi again entered service in the Direct-Duty Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi returned to duty in the Direct-Duty Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 辛未，徙臨賀王子產為南平王，晉熙王子輿為廬陵王。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Prince of Linhe Zichan was transferred to be Prince of Nanping, and Prince of Jinxi Ziyu was transferred to be Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Prince of Linhe Zichan was reassigned as Prince of Nanping, and Prince of Jinxi Ziyu as Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以尚書右僕射王景文為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On renshen, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jingwen was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jingwen was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 景文，即彧也，避上名，以字行。

translations.literal: Jingwen was in fact Yu, avoiding the emperor's tabooed name and going by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen was Wang Yu; to avoid the emperor's tabooed name, he used his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，追尊沈太妃曰宣太后，陵曰崇寧。

translations.literal: On yihai, Lady Shen the Consort was posthumously honored as Empress Xuan, and her tomb was named Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Prince of Xiangdong Yu's mother Lady Shen was posthumously honored as Empress Xuan, with a tomb named Chongning.

sentences.zh: 初，豫州刺史山陽王休祐入朝，以長史、南梁郡太守陳郡殷琰行府州事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Governor of Yu province Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou had entered court, and the Chief Clerk and Administrator of Nanliang commandery Yin Yan of Chen commandery acted in his stead in the province and commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Governor of Yu province Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou came to court, Chief Clerk and Administrator of Nanliang commandery Yin Yan of Chen commandery handled provincial affairs in his stead.

sentences.zh: 及休祐徙荊州，即以琰為督豫、司二州諸軍事、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xiuyou was transferred to Jing province, Yan was at once made Commander-in-Chief over all military affairs of Yu and Si provinces and Governor of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyou was reassigned to Jing province, Yan was made commander over Yu and Si provinces and Governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 有司奏路太后宜即前號，移居外宮；

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Empress Dowager Lu ought to assume her previous title and move to the outer palace;
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted that Empress Dowager Lu should revert to her former title and relocate to the outer palace;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，尊路太后為崇憲皇太后，居崇憲宮，供奉禮儀，不異舊日。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Empress Dowager Lu was honored as Grand Empress Dowager Chongxian, dwelt in the Chongxian Palace, and provisions and ceremonial honors were no different from former days.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Empress Dowager Lu was honored as Grand Empress Dowager Chongxian, housed in the Chongxian Palace with rites and provisions unchanged from before.

sentences.zh: 立妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Consort Wang was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang was made empress.

sentences.zh: 後，景文之妹也。

translations.literal: The empress was Jingwen's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: She was Wang Jingwen's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 罷二銖錢，禁鵝眼、綖環錢，餘皆通用。

translations.literal: The two-zhu coin was abolished; goose-eye and thread-ring coin were prohibited; the rest were all permitted for general circulation.
translations.idiomatic: The two-zhu coin was abolished; goose-eye and thread-ring cash were banned; all other coin remained legal tender.

sentences.zh: 江州佐吏得上所下令書，皆喜，共造鄧琬，曰：「暴亂既除，殿下又開黃閣，實為公私大慶。」

translations.literal: The Jiang province staff received the emperor's edicts of command and were all pleased; together they went to Deng Wan and said: "The violent turmoil has already been removed, and Your Highness has also opened the Yellow Pavilion—it is truly a great celebration for public and private alike."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiang province staff received the new emperor's edicts, they rejoiced and went together to Deng Wan, saying, "With the tyranny ended and Your Highness elevated to the Yellow Pavilion, this is cause for celebration all around."

sentences.zh: 琬以晉安王子勳次第居三，又以尋陽起事與世祖同符，謂事必有成，取令書投地曰：「殿下當開端門，黃閣是吾徒事耳！」

translations.literal: Wan, because Prince of Jin'an Zixun's order of birth was third and because the uprising at Xunyang matched the same omen as Emperor Shizu, believed the affair would surely succeed; he took the command document and threw it to the ground, saying: "Your Highness ought to open the End Gate—the Yellow Pavilion is a matter for the likes of us!"
translations.idiomatic: Wan noted that Prince of Jin'an Zixun was also third among his brothers, and that raising arms at Xunyang mirrored Emperor Xiaowu's own rise; convinced of success, he threw the edict to the ground and declared, "Your Highness should take the imperial gate—the Yellow Pavilion is our affair alone!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆駭愕。

translations.literal: All were startled and appalled.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly was stunned.

sentences.zh: 琬更與陶亮等繕治器甲，徵兵四方。

translations.literal: Wan thereupon, with Tao Liang and the others, repaired weapons and armor and raised troops from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wan then joined Tao Liang and others to gather arms and armor and levy troops throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 袁顗既至襄陽，即與咨議參軍劉胡繕修兵械，簡集士卒，詐稱被太皇太后令，使其起兵，即建牙馳檄，奉表勸子勳即大位。

translations.literal: Once Yuan Yi had reached Xiangyang, he at once, with Consultation Attendant Liu Hu, repaired military equipment, picked and assembled soldiers, falsely claimed to have received the Grand Empress Dowager's order to raise troops, immediately raised his banner and sent forth proclamations, and submitted a memorial urging Zixun to ascend the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Yi reached Xiangyang, he and Consultation Attendant Liu Hu readied arms, mustered troops, and falsely claimed authorization from the Grand Empress Dowager; they raised banners, issued proclamations, and memorialized urging Zixun to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，更以山陽王休祐為江州刺史，荊州刺史臨海王子頊即留本任。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was again made Governor of Jiang province, and Governor of Jing province Prince of Linhai Zixu remained in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou was reassigned as Governor of Jiang province, while Governor of Jing province Prince of Linhai Zixu kept his post.

sentences.zh: 先是，廢帝以邵陵王子元為湘州刺史，中兵參軍沈仲玉為道路行事，至鵲頭，聞尋陽兵起，不敢進。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Deposed Emperor had appointed Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan Governor of Xiang province, with Central Army Attendant Shen Zhongyu acting en route; when they reached Que Head, they heard that troops had risen at Xunyang and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Qianfei had appointed Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan Governor of Xiang province, with Central Army Attendant Shen Zhongyu handling affairs on the road; at Que Head they heard of the uprising at Xunyang and halted.

sentences.zh: 琬遣數百人劫迎之，令子勳建牙於桑尾，傳檄建康，稱：「孤志遵前典，黜幽陟明。」

translations.literal: Wan sent several hundred men to seize and welcome them, had Zixun raise his banner at Sangwei, and transmitted proclamations to Jiankang, saying: "This orphan's ambition follows the precedents of old—deposing the obscure and elevating the luminous."
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent several hundred men to seize and escort them, had Zixun raise his banner at Sangwei, and dispatched proclamations to Jiankang declaring, "I follow ancient precedent in deposing the unworthy and elevating the worthy."

sentences.zh: 又謂上「轎害明茂，篡竊天寶，干我昭穆，寡我兄弟。

translations.literal: He further told the emperor: "With treacherous assassination you harmed the bright and flourishing, usurped Heaven's mandate, violated our ancestral temples, and made our brothers few.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused the emperor: "Through treachery you destroyed the bright and flourishing, usurped the Mandate of Heaven, violated our ancestral rites, and slaughtered our brothers.

sentences.zh: 藐孤同氣，猶有十三，聖靈何辜，而當乏饗。」

translations.literal: Despising this orphan of one breath with the same qi, yet thirteen still remain—the sacred spirits what crime did they commit, that they should suffer want of sacrificial offerings?"
translations.idiomatic: You scorn this orphan who shares your blood, yet thirteen brothers still remain—what offense did our ancestral spirits commit, to be left without offerings?"

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史安陸王子緩承子勳初檄，欲攻廢帝；

translations.literal: Governor of Ying province Prince of Anlu Zihuan, on receiving Zixun's initial proclamation, wished to attack the Deposed Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Ying province Prince of Anlu Zihuan, on receiving Zixun's initial proclamation, prepared to attack Emperor Qianfei;

sentences.zh: 聞廢帝已隕，即解甲下標。

translations.literal: On hearing the Deposed Emperor had already fallen, he at once doffed his armor and lowered his banner.
translations.idiomatic: But learning Emperor Qianfei was already dead, he disbanded his forces and lowered his banners.

sentences.zh: 既而聞江、雍猶治兵，郢府行事苟卞之大懼，即遣咨議、領中兵參軍鄭景玄帥軍馳下，並送軍糧。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on hearing that Jiang and Yong provinces were still marshaling troops, the acting official of the Ying prefectural headquarters Gou Bianzhi was greatly afraid and at once sent Consultation Attendant and Central Army Attendant Concurrent Commander Zheng Jingxuan to lead troops rushing downstream, also sending military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, hearing that Jiang and Yong were still arming for war, the acting prefect of Ying Gou Bianzhi panicked and dispatched Consultation Attendant and Central Army Commander Zheng Jingxuan with troops downstream, along with military supplies.

sentences.zh: 荊州行事孔道存奉刺史臨海王子頊，會稽將佐奉太守尋陽王子房，皆舉兵以應子勳。

translations.literal: The acting official of Jing province Kong Daocun supported Governor Prince of Linhai Zixu, and the aides of Kuaiji supported Administrator Prince of Xunyang Zifang—all raised troops in response to Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Acting governor of Jing Kong Daocun rallied behind Governor Prince of Linhai Zixu, and Kuaiji's officials backed Prefect Prince of Xunyang Zifang—all took up arms for Zixun.
